items.category: SRX Fleming Broadcom TD3/SDK, datapath related issue
items.synopsis: On some SRX platforms configuring global-mode switching where 1G SFP is used on 10G port causes port to go down
items.description: On SRX1600, SRX2300 and SRX4300 platforms, upon configuring "set protocols l2-learning global-mode switching" where 1G SFP is used on 10G port the port goes down after sometime causing traffic drop. This traffic drop is only subjected to the port where the configuration is applied, thus the other ports remains unaffected.

items.synopsis: Major alarms for fabric link faults that result in reduced fabric capacity are introduced on PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line cards and SF5 fabric, fabric link faults need to be reported as major alarms. Link faults can occur during system operation and result in reduced fabric capacity with partial impact. This enhancement introduces the new alarm "One or more PFE pairs operating with less than acceptable fabric capacity" to indicate reduced fabric capacity conditions.

items.synopsis: Multicast traffic from source connected to PEG device that is PIM Non-DR in IRB interface of SBD is not forwarded to the receivers connected to SL devices
items.description: Multicast traffic from source connected to PEG (PIM EVPN Gateway) device that is PIM Non-DR in IRB interface of SBD (Supplemental Bridge Domain) is not forwarded to the receivers connected to SL (Server Leaf) devices. The problem impacts only EX5200 platforms, the other platforms are not impacted.

items.synopsis: PFE process crash occurs during EX4k boot-up
items.description: On EX4400/4100 platforms, PFE process (fxpc) crash occurs with a segmentation fault (SIGSEGV) during device boot-up. The crash occurs during the Broadcom PHY firmware broadcast download sequence when initializing the external PHY. No service impact as this crash happens at initial boot cycle.

items.synopsis: An operationally down interface might trigger "DPDK port is stuck with hardware issue!!!" error log
items.description: On SRX4100 and SRX4200, if a physical interface that transitions to the operationally down state and remains down during the next 60-second, Data Plane Development Kit (DPDK) monitoring cycle might be incorrectly reported as transmit (Tx) stuck. This condition triggers a Flexible PIC Concentrator (FPC) major alarm and redundancy group failover if you configure the chassis cluster, which might result in temporary traffic disruption. The issue is resolved by excluding operationally down interfaces from DPDK Tx-stuck monitoring.

items.synopsis: ISSU will abort on EX-4400, EX-4100 and EX-4000 if any ISSU incompatible configurations are detected on the device.
items.description: During ISSU image validation, SW will now check for any ISSU incompatible configurations configured on the device.

items.synopsis: File copy CLI command fails to resolve remote hostnames when no username is specified
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when copying a file to a remote host using a hostname, the device is unable to resolve the hostname, causing the file transfer to fail. Secure Copy (SCP) operations are not affected and continue to work as expected. This issue does not impact network services or device functionality.

items.synopsis: Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms experience an mgd process crash when a user assigned to a login class with 'no-hidden-commands' requests CLI help for a single-word command
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, when a user assigned to a login class configured with 'no-hidden-commands' requests CLI help for a single-word command, such as 'clear?', the mgd process crashes. The CLI session that triggers the issue is terminated, but other user sessions and traffic forwarding are not affected. The system recovers automatically, and the affected user can establish a new CLI session.

items.synopsis: Event script fails during a virtual chassis role change
items.description: Event script failure occurs during a virtual chassis primary role change when the system is unable to load a required component at the time the script is executed.

items.synopsis: Major alarms for fabric link faults that result in reduced fabric capacity are introduced on PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms
items.description: On Junos OS Evolved PTX10004 and PTX10008 platforms with LC1301 line cards and SF5 fabric, fabric link faults need to be reported as major alarms. Link faults can occur during system operation and result in reduced fabric capacity with partial impact. This enhancement introduces the new alarm "One or more PFE pairs operating with less than acceptable fabric capacity" to indicate reduced fabric capacity conditions.

items.synopsis: Incorrect high-temperature readings trigger chassis shutdown
items.description: An incorrect high-temperature reading from the Intake-B temperature sensor on MX10004 and MX10008 systems running Junos OS with LC9600 line cards triggers an over-temperature condition and causes an automatic chassis shutdown. This results in a complete service outage that requires manual intervention to restore service.

items.synopsis: The rpd process crashes when deleting BGP VPN routing instances during an active SNMP walk on the RIB
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms, rpd process crash is caused by deleting a routing-instances of type Virtual Routing and Forwarding (VRF) while a Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) walk operation is in progress.

items.synopsis: Inserted SFB is not correctly shown in "show chassis" output on MX2020/MX2010
items.description: On the MX2020/MX2010 platforms, when inserting SFB into empty slot and didn't issue "request chassis sfb slot online", some variants of "show chassis" command cannot correctly show the info of target SFB. After issuing "request chassis sfb offline" and re-inserting the SFB, the i2c_data_sent flag is never set because the SFB is not scheduled for power-on in that path. As a result, chassisd never receives the I2C/IDEEPROM data and the SFB does not appear as "Present" in show chassis hardware models / show chassis environment sfb. There is no service impact.

items.synopsis: ENTITY-MIB returns incorrect hardware containment information for SFP Optics
items.description: On Junos OS platforms, devices return incorrect information in response to queries for SFP (Small Form-factor Pluggable) inventory and hierarchy levels when data is retrieved using the standard SNMP MIB (Simple Network Management Protocol Management Information Base). As a result, the ENTITY-MIB object 'entPhysicalContainedIn' can report an incorrect parent hardware component for SFP optics

items.synopsis: Tunnel interface flaps observed on every DNS TTL refresh when FQDN is used as the destination of IP-IP tunnel and the ip-0/0/0 interface is in a routing-instance
items.description: On Junos OS SRX platforms, when FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) is used for the destination of IP-IP (Internet Protocol-in-Internet Protocol) tunnel and the ip-0/0/0 interface is in a routing-instance, the ip-0/0/0 interface flaps every time the SRX sends DNS (Domain Name System) query. The issue is caused by a timing condition between rpd (Routing Protocol Daemon) and dcd (Device Control Daemon) during DNS (Domain Name System) re-resolution, resulting in tunnel interface flaps, leading to packet loss.

items.synopsis: False Routing Software Alarms Triggered by Incorrect Bridge Domain Classification as Multicast VXLAN
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved, if Virtual Local Area Networks (VLANs) configured in a Media Access Control Virtual Routing and Forwarding (MAC-VRF) instance with Virtual Extensible Local Area Network (VXLAN) are not included in the associated protocols evpn vni-list, the system incorrectly identifies the corresponding Bridge Domains (BDs) as multicast VXLAN bridge domains. This behavior can result in unnecessary Virtualized Multi-Homing Enhanced (VMENH) next-hop creation and trigger a false routing software alarm

items.synopsis: Local MAC addresses are not learned on newly added EVPN all-active interfaces
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved systems configured with Ethernet VPN (EVPN) Media Access Control Virtual Private Network (MAC-VRF) over Multiprotocol Label Switching (MPLS), when a new all-active interface is added to a service that uses a VLAN-aware instance with interfaces from multiple Ethernet Segments (ESIs) and Egress Link Protection (ELP) enabled, local Media Access Control (MAC) addresses are not learned on the newly added interface. As a result, Layer 2 forwarding for the affected service is impacted and complete loss of Layer 2 forwarding can occur for the affected service. Service can be restored by restarting the affected routing application

items.synopsis: EX5200: During repeated pic offline/online events on p2a 8x25g ULM with 25g and 10g optics, one or more of the 25g interfaces are not coming up and remain in down state.
items.description: In an EX5200 device with 8x25G uplink module (ULM) inserted, during repeated pic 2 offline/online operation, in some instances random 25G ports which have explicit FEC config, may stay operational down state. The workaround is to reapply the FEC configuration.

items.synopsis: False alarms related to PoE Device Manager failures were observed on EX4100
items.description: On EX4100-F-24P and EX4100-24P platforms, while running 26.2R1 Junos release, PoE (Power over Ethernet) device manager failed alarms observed for PoE manager 3 to 11 without any triggers. These PoE device managers does not exist physically in these platforms. The actual PoE device managers are 0, 1 and 2. The alarms are cosmetic and there is no operational impact. These alarms can be ignored.

items.synopsis: Unexpected FPC reboot in QFX device after inserting and removing a transceiver
items.description: On Junos QFX10002-60C/QFX10008/QFX10016 an unexpected FPC reboot with dcpfe core dump is experienced due to a transceiver plug-in plug-out in an Aggregated Ethernet (AE) interface member affecting all traffic on that line card. No manual intervention is required, fpc will automatically reboot and recover

items.synopsis: RG1 failover is not automatically triggered after fan failures on SRX4100/SRX4200 chassis clusters, resulting in traffic degradation
items.description: On SRX4100 and SRX4200 chassis clusters, when all chassis fans fail or are removed, the affected node continues forwarding traffic in a degraded thermal state instead of automatically triggering a Redundancy Group 1 (RG1) failover. This result in the traffic loss on the affected node.

items.synopsis: The dhcpd crash triggered by DHCPv6 ALQ peer state inconsistency
items.description: On MX104, MX204, MX240, MX301, MX304, MX480, MX960, MX2008, MX2010, MX2020, MX10003, MX10004, MX10008 and MX10016 platforms DHCPv6 (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol version 6) ALQ (Active Lease Query) peer state inconsistency creates an invalid subscriber entry for a bound IPv6 address, resulting in a jdhcpd (Junos DHCP daemon) crash with recurring core dumps and subscriber traffic impact.

items.synopsis: [mx10008] ND probes for static MAC-IP EVPN entries are sourced from wrongly built EUI-64 link-local addresses
items.description: The EUI-64 link-local address construction in l2alm_irb_local_addr() was missing the mandatory 0xFF, 0xFE byte insertion at positions 3-4 of the interface identifier. After bzero, bytes 3-4 remained 0x00, 0x00, causing NS probes for static MAC-IP entries to use a malformed source address. For example, in problem state, IPv6 link-local address is fe80:: 2293:3900:eb:f44a, derived as follows: IRB MAC: 20:93:39:eb:f4:4a Buggy - before fix - bytes 3-4 left as 00:00 after bzero: [20 | 0x02] 93 39 : 00 00 : eb f4 4a [00 00 is inserted between 2 halves of MAC address] -> fe80:: 2293:3900:eb:f44a [above result is prefixed with fe80:: ] After fix: [20 | 0x02] 93 39 : ff fe : eb f4 4a [FF FE is inserted between 2 halves of MAC address] -> fe80:: 2293:39ff:feeb:f44a [above result is prefixed with fe80:: ]

items.synopsis: Crash in the rpd process after LDP P2MP LSP Identifier reaches its maximum value and rolls over, due to duplicate identifier allocation
items.description: On all Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved versions that support Label Distribution Protocol Point-to-Multipoint Label Switched Paths (LDP P2MP LSPs), the rpd process (routing protocol daemon) crashes when an LSP Identifier reaches its 24-bit maximum value (224 1 = 16, 777, 215) and rolls over to the starting value because a duplicate identifier is incorrectly allocated. This condition occurs only after prolonged tunnel flapping (typically more than 16 million flaps). When the rpd process crashes, routing convergence is briefly disrupted, and services relying on label-switched traffic are impacted until the process automatically restarts.

items.category: JDHCP is a daemon for EVO platform to handle DHCP protocol
items.synopsis: On Junos Evolved OS ACX platforms loss of subscriber bindings can disrupt DHCPv6 redundancy synchronization in relay/server HA setups configured with ALQ/BLQ
items.description: On Junos Evolved OS ACX platforms configured in High Availability (HA) mode with ALQ/BLQ(Active lease query/Bulk lease query) enabled, a DHCP process crash occur when a customer edge (CE) device sends DHCPv6 IA_NA (Identity Association for Non-Temporary Address) and IA_PD (Identity Association for Prefix Delegation) requests in separate SOLICIT messages, and the requests are processed by different HA peers. This result in loss of the subscriber binding and disrupt DHCPv6 redundancy synchronisation on the relay/server.

items.synopsis: PFE crash due to memory corruption when STP is enabled
items.description: On all Junos Platforms, a rare memory corruption condition may occur in the Packet Forwarding Engine (PFE) when Spanning Tree Protocol (STP) is enabled and operating in default (distributed) mode. When the issue is triggered, the PFE crashes and a dc-pfe core file is generated. The exact trigger for the memory corruption is currently unknown.

items.synopsis: Duplicate egress VLAN-translation entry additions in VXLAN configurations cause a forwarding-plane memory leak on QFX5K and EX4K switches
items.description: On affected QFX5K and EX4K switches running classic Junos OS, this issue occurs when VXLAN with egress VLAN translation is configured and an egress VLAN-translation entry is repeatedly added while a matching entry already exists. During normal operation, the memory allocated for this operation is released after the existing entry is detected. Due to this issue, the forwarding-plane memory allocated during each duplicate-entry addition is not released, causing memory consumption to accumulate. When the available forwarding-plane memory is exhausted, the FPC restarts while the Routing Engine remains operational. All interfaces on the affected FPC flap, and traffic is interrupted during the restart.

items.category: QFX5K JUNOS Interface, MACSec, Optics, SDK, PHY
items.synopsis: The dcpfe process crash observed during a system reboot or PFE restart when software-based linkscan is configured
items.description: On QFX5120-48Y, QFX5120-48T, QFX5120-32C and EX4650 platforms, a system reboot or PFE restart after configuring software-based linkscan causes the dcpfe process to crash. As a result, traffic forwarding on interfaces associated with the affected FPC will be temporarily impacted during the recovery period.

items.synopsis: The rpd process consumes high CPU when an aggregate route temporarily loses all active contributors with OC-TLV support enabled
items.description: On Junos OS and Junos OS Evolved platforms supporting OC-TLV, the rpd process may experience sustained high CPU utilization when OC-TLV support is enabled, and an aggregate route temporarily loses all active contributing routes. A minor CPU hog alarm for the rpd process will be reported. This high CPU utilization subsequently compromises other system processes and protocols, leading to an impact on the traffic.

items.category: Issues related route resolution routing infrastructure
items.synopsis: Service route is hidden over BGP LU multipath upon neighbor route withdrawn
items.description: On all Junos and Junos Evolved platforms, the following condition is a prerequisite - Service route resolving over BGP LU (Border Gateway Protocol Labeled Unicast) multipath route with multipath resolve policy enabled. The issue occurs when one BGP LU neighbour withdraws its route. This withdrawal causes the top-level service route to temporarily become hidden, and then it reappears after re-resolving over the remaining BGP LU multipath routes. However, after this recovery, the BGP LU resolution changes from multipath to single path.This behavior results in a brief traffic loss during the interval when the service route is hidden and then restored.

items.synopsis: RSVP LSP traffic loss during primary path recovery with setup-protection
items.description: On Junos and Junos OS Evolved platforms, Resource Reservation Protocol (RSVP) Label-Switched Paths (LSPs) using facility backup(setup-protection) experience a temporary traffic disruption when the primary path recovers and local reversion is enabled. The issue occurs when the LSP is signaled through a non-Junos ingress router and the administrative group constraints of the bypass LSP change. The affected LSP is resignaled during primary path recovery and traffic is disrupted for a few seconds before the LSP recovers automatically.

items.synopsis: Traffic loss on MX960 after chassis zone power failure
items.description: On MX960 platforms, a complete power failure in either chassis zone can cause all fabric planes to become inactive, resulting in complete traffic loss. The issue occurs because remote destination errors are misidentified as local errors by online Flexible PIC Concentrators (FPCs), causing all planes being removed from spray.

items.category: Remote Access VPN issues on SRX
items.synopsis: JSC SAML authentication fails when SRX HTTPS service is configured on a custom port
items.description: On SRX platforms, remote-access user authentication for the Juniper Secure Connect (JSC) client using Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) failed when the Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure (HTTPS) service under the Hypertext Transfer Protocol Daemon (httpd) was configured on a custom port instead of the standard port 443.

items.synopsis: Heap memory leak causing new subscriber login failures on deployments using PPPoE subscriber policer
items.description: On Junos OS MX Series platforms, when firewall filters with policer actions are applied to PPPoE subscriber interfaces through dynamic profiles, repeated PPPoE subscriber logout and login events cause memory leak of 16 to 64 bytes during policer event which is not noticeable in low-scale environments. In large BNG (Broadband Network Gateway) deployments, the leaked memory accumulates over time, leading to FPC (Flexible PIC Concentrator) heap memory growth. Once memory utilization exceeds operational thresholds, new PPPoE subscriber login attempts fail.
